message.content:
Draft a COMPLETE plan for backend/scripts/seed-dev-content.ts — a synthetic Prisma seed script that materializes 50 stories + 8 series (with 3-8 chapters each) for dev-only stress-testing of the recently-shipped GSAP animations (PRs #187–#191) on Lucifer's Diary.

Requirements:

VOLUME: 50 standalone Story rows, 8 Series rows with 3-8 chapters each (so ~40-60 total chapters).

SAFETY GUARDS (non-negotiable):
- Requires explicit `--confirm=dev` CLI flag; running without it prints a warning and exits with code 1.
- Requires `LUCIFER_ENV=dev` env var to be set. Without it the script refuses to run.
- Each seeded row is marked with a discoverable token (recommend: in a dedicated field if one exists, or as a known prefix like `[seed-dev]` in the title — pick the cleaner option based on schema).
- Idempotent: rerunning the script does NOT duplicate rows. Either detects existing seed rows (by marker) and refuses, or skips them.
- Supports `--purge` flag that wipes ONLY rows matching the marker (no other rows touched).
- Supports `--dry-run` flag that prints exactly what WOULD insert (counts + first few titles) without actually writing to the DB.

CONTENT GENERATION (the key constraint: no copyrighted material reproduced anywhere):
- Titles: faker-driven with a literary-evocative twist. Approach: combine word-pools from faker.word.* with hand-curated mood words (suggestive but not explicit) — e.g. `${faker.word.adjective()} ${moodNoun}` or `The ${noun} of ${faker.person.firstName()}`. Output should sound brand-appropriate (think evocative literary titles, not graphic).
- Excerpts: faker.lorem.sentences(3) modified to sound moody — prepend with one of a small pool of evocative openers. 100% original (faker-generated), not derived from any source.
- Bodies: pure faker.lorem.paragraphs() — varied length from ~500 to ~10,000 words. Animation testing doesn't care what the body says, only how long it is.
- Tags: read the existing tag taxonomy from the DB at script-runtime via prisma.tag.findMany(), pick 3-6 random tags per row weighted to include both safe and adult tags. Mix should match real-site distribution roughly.
- isAuthorsChoice: 5% probability per story/chapter.
- publishedAt: spread across the last 6 months, random.
- Series.status: weighted mix of ONGOING / COMPLETE / HIATUS.
- estimatedReadMinutes: computed from body word count.

Report via SYNTHETIC_PLAN_SCHEMA. The codeSkeleton field should be a real TypeScript draft (~150-250 lines) showing argument parsing, env-guard, prisma lifecycle, content generators, tag-selection algorithm, marker logic, purge logic, dry-run logic — enough to commit and refine, not pseudo-code. Use the project-inventory findings (faker version, schema shape, script convention) — the synthesizer agent will pass them in via context.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. - simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

14	// ============================================================
15	// TAGS
16	// ============================================================
17	
18	model Tag {
19	  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
20	  name      String   @unique
21	  // URL-safe slug computed from the name on write. Used by the public
22	  // /tag/[slug] route so tag URLs don't expose UUIDs and so they
23	  // survive a tag rename gracefully (the slug rewrites along with
24	  // the name).
25	  slug      String   @unique
26	  // Marks a tag as adult/NSFW. Stories and chapters carrying any adult
27	  // tag get the NSFW gate before reading. Computed on the fly from this
28	  // flag — there is no separate isAdult column on content.
29	  isAdult   Boolean  @default(false) @map("is_adult")
30	  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
31	
32	  storyTags   StoryTag[]
33	  seriesTags  SeriesTag[]
34	  chapterTags ChapterTag[]
35	
36	  @@map("tags")
37	}
38	
39	// ============================================================
40	// STORIES (standalone)
41	// ============================================================
42	
43	model Story {
44	  id                     String                   @id @default(uuid())
45	  title                  String
46	  content                String // full text, paginated at query time
47	  excerpt                String
48	  // Optional one- or two-line passage rendered before the body in
49	  // italic, centered. Standard literary-fiction device — quote, verse,
50	  // dedication, etc.
51	  epigraph               String?
52	  estimatedReadMinutes   Int                      @map("estimated_read_minutes")
53	  accumulatedReadSeconds BigInt                   @default(0) @map("accumulated_read_seconds")
54	  likeCount              Int                      @default(0) @map("like_count")
55	  isAuthorsChoice        Boolean                  @default(false) @map("is_authors_choice")
56	  authorsNote            String?                  @map("authors_note")
57	  publishedAt            DateTime?                @map("published_at")
58	  createdAt              DateTime                 @default(now()) @map("created_at")
59	  updatedAt              DateTime                 @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
60	  // Soft-delete timestamp (audit M-07). Set when admin clicks
61	  // Delete; reads filter `deletedAt: null` via a Prisma middleware.
62	  // A scheduled cron in cleanup.service.ts hard-deletes rows whose
63	  // deletedAt is older than the retention window, doing the
64	  // polymorphic Like/Save/Session cleanup at the same time.
65	  deletedAt              DateTime?                @map("deleted_at")
66	  // Generated tsvector — Postgres-maintained, queried via $queryRaw
67	  // with websearch_to_tsquery; never read through the Prisma client.
68	  // Modeled Unsupported so migrate dev keeps it.
69	  searchVector           Unsupported("tsvector")? @map("search_vector")
70	
71	  tags  StoryTag[]
72	  // Multi-card admin scratchpad. Each Note is one pill in the editor's
73	  // Notes panel; color-coded. Private — never returned by any public
74	  // reader endpoint. Replaced the legacy `notes String?` field; the
75	  // 20260608*_add_notes_model migration carries old content forward.
76	  notes Note[]
77	
78	  @@index([deletedAt])
79	  @@map("stories")
80	}
81	
82	// ============================================================
83	// SERIES
84	// ============================================================
85	
86	model Series {
87	  id                     String                   @id @default(uuid())
88	  title                  String
89	  excerpt                String
90	  // Optional series-level preface — surfaces on the series page above
91	  // the chapter list. Mirrors the authors_note field already present
92	  // on Story and Chapter so the three content types stay aligned.
93	  authorsNote            String?                  @map("authors_note")
94	  // Reader-facing status — lets readers know whether more chapters
95	  // are coming. Defaults to ONGOING for new series; flipped to
96	  // COMPLETE once the work is finished, HIATUS for paused series.
97	  status                 SeriesStatus             @default(ONGOING)
98	  accumulatedReadSeconds BigInt                   @default(0) @map("accumulated_read_seconds")
99	  likeCount              Int                      @default(0) @map("like_count")
100	  createdAt              DateTime                 @default(now()) @map("created_at")
101	  updatedAt              DateTime                 @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

105	  deletedAt              DateTime?                @map("deleted_at")

108	  searchVector           Unsupported("tsvector")? @map("search_vector")

111	  tags     SeriesTag[]
112	  follows  Follow[]
113	
114	  @@index([deletedAt])
115	  @@map("series")
116	}
117	
118	enum SeriesStatus {

120	  COMPLETE
121	  HIATUS
122	}
123

125	// CHAPTERS
126	// ============================================================
127

129	  id                     String                   @id @default(uuid())
130	  seriesId               String                   @map("series_id")

132	  content                String
133	  excerpt                String
134	  // Optional one- or two-line passage rendered before the body in
135	  // italic, centered. Mirrors Story.epigraph.
136	  epigraph               String?
137	  orderIndex             Int                      @map("order_index")
138	  estimatedReadMinutes   Int                      @map("estimated_read_minutes")
139	  isAuthorsChoice        Boolean                  @default(false) @map("is_authors_choice")
140	  authorsNote            String?                  @map("authors_note")
141	  accumulatedReadSeconds BigInt                   @default(0) @map("accumulated_read_seconds")
142	  likeCount              Int                      @default(0) @map("like_count")
143	  publishedAt            DateTime?                @map("published_at")
144	  createdAt              DateTime                 @default(now()) @map("created_at")
145	  updatedAt              DateTime                 @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
146	  // Soft-delete timestamp — see Story.deletedAt. Soft-deleting a

148	  // owns; soft-deleting an individual chapter only touches that row.
149	  deletedAt              DateTime?                @map("deleted_at")
150	  // Generated tsvector — see Story.searchVector for the contract.
151	  searchVector           Unsupported("tsvector")? @map("search_vector")
152	
153	  series Series       @relation(fields: [seriesId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
154	  tags   ChapterTag[]
155	  // Multi-card admin scratchpad — see Story.notes for the contract.
156	  notes  Note[]
157	
158	  @@index([seriesId, orderIndex])
159	  @@index([deletedAt])
160	  @@map("chapters")
161	}
162	
163	// ============================================================
164	// JUNCTION TABLES (tags)
165	// ============================================================
166	
167	model StoryTag {
168	  storyId String @map("story_id")
169	  tagId   String @map("tag_id")
170	
171	  story Story @relation(fields: [storyId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
172	  tag   Tag   @relation(fields: [tagId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
173	
174	  @@id([storyId, tagId])
175	  @@map("story_tags")
176	}
177	
178	model SeriesTag {
179	  seriesId String @map("series_id")
180	  tagId    String @map("tag_id")
181	
182	  series Series @relation(fields: [seriesId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
183	  tag    Tag    @relation(fields: [tagId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
184	
185	  @@id([seriesId, tagId])
186	  @@map("series_tags")
187	}
188	
189	model ChapterTag {
190	  chapterId String @map("chapter_id")
191	  tagId     String @map("tag_id")
192	
193	  chapter Chapter @relation(fields: [chapterId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
194	  tag     Tag     @relation(fields: [tagId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
195	
196	  @@id([chapterId, tagId])
197	  @@map("chapter_tags")
198	}
199	
200	// ============================================================
201	// LIKES (anonymous + user-bound)
202	// ============================================================
203	//
204	// content_type is either "story" or "chapter".
205	// content_id is the UUID of the story or chapter.
206	//
207	// Each like row is owned by EITHER an anonymous reader (sessionToken
208	// from localStorage) OR a logged-in user (userId), never both. A
209	// CHECK constraint on the table enforces this. Two partial unique
210	// indexes prevent the same owner from liking the same content twice
211	// — one for sessionToken, one for userId — and they're added in the
212	// migration since Prisma doesn't model partial uniques.
213	//
214	// We deliberately keep both columns rather than migrating anonymous
215	// likes to userId on first login, so a reader's prior likes survive
216	// alongside their account-bound likes.
217	// ============================================================
218	
219	// Polymorphic — contentId references either stories.id or chapters.id depending on
220	// contentType. We deliberately don't model this as a foreign key in Prisma because
221	// a single column can't be FK-bound to two parent tables (every insert would try
222	// to satisfy both constraints and fail). Cleanup of orphaned likes when a story
223	// or chapter is deleted is handled at the service layer.
224	model Like {
225	  id           String   @id @default(uuid())
226	  contentType  String   @map("content_type")
227	  contentId    String   @map("content_id")
228	  sessionToken String?  @map("session_token")
229	  userId       String?  @map("user_id")
230	  createdAt    DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
231	
232	  user User? @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
233	
234	  @@index([contentType, contentId])
235	  @@index([userId])
236	  @@map("likes")
237	}
238	
239	// ============================================================
240	// READ SESSIONS (anonymous time tracking)
241	// ============================================================
242	//
243	// When a visitor leaves a reading page the browser sends time spent.
244	// If time_spent_seconds >= 50% of estimated_read_minutes * 60, qualified = true.
245	// On qualification, accumulated_read_seconds on the story/chapter is incremented.
246	// Unique constraint prevents one visitor from contributing more than once per content.
247	// ============================================================
248	
249	// ============================================================
250	// USERS
251	// ============================================================
252	//
253	// Username + password only. No email at signup, no recovery flow —
254	// "if you forget, you're on your own." The email column is reserved
255	// for an opt-in sync feature shipped in a later PR. lastActiveAt is
256	// bumped on authenticated requests and feeds the silent inactivity-
257	// deletion cron: an account whose lastActiveAt is older than
258	// (now - deletionPeriodDays) is dropped without warning.
259	// ============================================================
260	
261	model User {
262	  id                 String    @id @default(uuid())
263	  username           String    @unique
264	  passwordHash       String    @map("password_hash")
265	  // Reserved for the optional-email-sync feature (later PR). Nullable
266	  // by design; many users may never set one. emailVerifyToken is a
267	  // one-shot token written when the user first sets / changes their
268	  // email and consumed by the verification endpoint.
269	  email              String?   @unique
270	  emailVerifiedAt    DateTime? @map("email_verified_at")
271	  emailVerifyToken   String?   @map("email_verify_token")
272	  // Reader-configurable in the settings tab. Default 1 year.
273	  deletionPeriodDays Int       @default(365) @map("deletion_period_days")
274	  lastActiveAt       DateTime  @default(now()) @map("last_active_at")
275	  createdAt          DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
276	  updatedAt          DateTime  @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
277	
278	  likes        Like[]
279	  savedContent SavedContent[]
280	  follows      Follow[]
281	
282	  @@index([lastActiveAt])
283	  @@map("users")
284	}
285	
286	// ============================================================
287	// FOLLOWS (logged-in users following a series)
288	// ============================================================
289	//
290	// Composite primary key on (userId, seriesId) — one row per pair.
291	// `lastSeenAt` is bumped when the user opens their dashboard; new
292	// chapters published after that timestamp surface as "unread" until
293	// the next visit.
294	// ============================================================
295	
296	model Follow {
297	  userId     String   @map("user_id")
298	  seriesId   String   @map("series_id")
299	  lastSeenAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("last_seen_at")
300	  createdAt  DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
301	
302	  user   User   @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
303	  series Series @relation(fields: [seriesId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
304	
305	  @@id([userId, seriesId])
306	  @@index([seriesId])
307	  @@map("follows")
308	}
309	
310	// ============================================================
311	// SAVED CONTENT (logged-in users only)
312	// ============================================================
313	//
314	// User's bookmark list. Polymorphic — see Like for why content_id
315	// doesn't have parent FKs. One row per (user, content) pair: the
316	// unique index makes "save" idempotent.
317	// ============================================================
318	
319	model SavedContent {
320	  id          String   @id @default(uuid())
321	  userId      String   @map("user_id")
322	  contentType String   @map("content_type")
323	  contentId   String   @map("content_id")
324	  createdAt   DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
325	
326	  user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
327	
328	  @@unique([userId, contentType, contentId])
329	  @@index([contentType, contentId])
330	  @@index([userId])
331	  @@map("saved_content")
332	}
333	
334	// Polymorphic — see comment on Like for why this doesn't have parent FKs.
335	model ReadSession {
336	  id               String   @id @default(uuid())
337	  contentType      String   @map("content_type")
338	  contentId        String   @map("content_id")
339	  sessionToken     String   @map("session_token")
340	  timeSpentSeconds Int      @map("time_spent_seconds")
341	  qualified        Boolean  @default(false)
342	  createdAt        DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
343	
344	  @@unique([contentType, contentId, sessionToken])
345	  @@index([contentType, contentId])
346	  @@map("read_sessions")
347	}
348	
349	// ============================================================
350	// READING POSITIONS (continue where you left off)
351	// ============================================================
352	//
353	// One row per (content × reader). On scroll the frontend posts a
354	// scrollPercentage 0–100 plus the current pageNumber for paginated
355	// reads. On revisit the chapter / story page auto-scrolls to the
356	// stored position.
357	//
358	// `identifier` is either a `userId` (logged-in) or a `sessionToken`
359	// (anonymous); `identifierType` disambiguates. Mirrors the Like
360	// row's split between sessionToken / userId, but keeping the two
361	// values in a single column gives us a clean composite unique
362	// constraint — readers can hold at most one position per content
363	// regardless of where they're authenticated.
364	//
365	// Auto-purge after 180 days lives in cleanup.service.ts.
366	model ReadingPosition {
367	  id               String   @id @default(uuid())
368	  contentType      String   @map("content_type")
369	  contentId        String   @map("content_id")
370	  identifier       String
371	  identifierType   String   @map("identifier_type")
372	  scrollPercentage Float    @map("scroll_percentage")
373	  pageNumber       Int?     @map("page_number")
374	  lastSeenAt       DateTime @default(now()) @updatedAt @map("last_seen_at")
375	  createdAt        DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
376	
377	  @@unique([contentType, contentId, identifier, identifierType])
378	  @@index([identifier, identifierType, lastSeenAt(sort: Desc)])
379	  @@index([contentType, contentId])
380	  @@map("reading_positions")
381	}
382	
383	// ============================================================
384	// ADMIN AUDIT LOG (audit L-02)
385	// ============================================================
386	//
387	// One row per admin-authenticated mutation (POST / PATCH / DELETE
388	// on any route that passed JwtAuthGuard). Lets us answer "what
389	// changed and when?" after an incident — e.g. "story 'xyz' is
390	// gone, who deleted it?" The interceptor that writes this lives
391	// at `common/interceptors/admin-audit.interceptor.ts`.
392	//
393	// `metadata` is a free-form JSON column for extra context per
394	// action (HTTP method, URL, response status, bulk operation
395	// counts). Keeping it untyped means we can add new fields in
396	// service code without further migrations.
397	model AdminAuditLog {
398	  id          String   @id @default(uuid())
399	  action      String
400	  entityType  String?  @map("entity_type")
401	  entityId    String?  @map("entity_id")
402	  method      String
403	  path        String
404	  statusCode  Int      @map("status_code")
405	  metadata    Json?
406	  performedAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("performed_at")
407	
408	  @@index([entityType, entityId])
409	  @@index([performedAt])
410	  @@map("admin_audit_log")
411	}
412	
413	// ============================================================
414	// NOTES (admin scratchpad — multi-card, color-coded)
415	// ============================================================
416	//
417	// Each Note is one card in the admin Notes panel on the
418	// Story / Chapter editor. Replaces the legacy single-string
419	// `notes` column previously on Story and Chapter. Polymorphic
420	// owner — exactly one of storyId / chapterId is set, enforced
421	// in the migration via a CHECK constraint (Prisma can't model
422	// XOR-nullable FKs directly).
423	
424	model Note {
425	  id         String    @id @default(uuid())
426	  storyId    String?   @map("story_id")
427	  chapterId  String?   @map("chapter_id")
428	  // Short pill title — shown collapsed in the panel.
429	  title      String    @default("")
430	  // Body of the note. Plain text — see Story.notes (legacy) for
431	  // why we don't drag a rich-text editor in here.
432	  body       String    @default("")
433	  // Pill / dot color in the admin Notes panel. Enum keeps the
434	  // palette tight and validated; adding a color is a one-line
435	  // schema change (each addition needs a migration).
436	  color      NoteColor @default(GOLD)
437	  // Sort order within the owner's notes list. Lower first. Drag-
438	  // to-reorder is future work; today new notes append.
439	  orderIndex Int       @default(0) @map("order_index")
440	  createdAt  DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
441	  updatedAt  DateTime  @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
442	
443	  story   Story?   @relation(fields: [storyId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
444	  chapter Chapter? @relation(fields: [chapterId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
445	
446	  @@index([storyId, orderIndex])
447	  @@index([chapterId, orderIndex])
448	  @@map("notes")
449	}
450	
451	enum NoteColor {
452	  GOLD
453	  CRIMSON
454	  SAGE
455	  INDIGO
456	  AMBER
457	  SLATE
458	}

237	let token: string;
238	
239	async function api<T>(
240	  path: string,
241	  init: RequestInit = {},
242	): Promise<T> {
243	  const res = await fetch(`${API_URL}${path}`, {
244	    ...init,
245	    headers: {
246	      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
247	      ...(token ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } : {}),
248	      ...(init.headers ?? {}),
249	    },
250	  });
251	  if (!res.ok) {
252	    const text = await res.text().catch(() => '');
253	    throw new Error(`${init.method ?? 'GET'} ${path} -> ${res.status}: ${text}`);
254	  }
255	  if (res.status === 204) return undefined as T;
256	  return (await res.json()) as T;
257	}

259	async function main() {
260	  // 1. Login
261	  console.log('Logging in...');
262	  const login = await api<{ access_token: string }>(`/auth/login`, {
263	    method: 'POST',

265	  });
266	  token = login.access_token;
267	
268	  // 2. Pull all tags
269	  console.log('Loading tags...');
270	  const tags = await api<ApiTag[]>(`/admin/tags`);
271	  const tagsByName = new Map(tags.map((t) => [t.name.toLowerCase(), t]));
272	
273	  const resolveTagIds = (names: string[]): string[] => {
274	    const ids: string[] = [];
275	    for (const name of names) {
276	      const tag = tagsByName.get(name.toLowerCase());
277	      if (!tag) {
278	        console.warn(`  ! tag not found: "${name}" — skipping`);
279	        continue;
280	      }
281	      ids.push(tag.id);
282	    }
283	    return ids;
284	  };
285	
286	  // 2b. Pull existing stories + series so we can skip what's already there.
287	  const [existingStories, existingSeries] = await Promise.all([
288	    api<{ id: string; title: string }[]>('/admin/stories'),
289	    api<{ id: string; title: string }[]>('/admin/series'),
290	  ]);
291	  const existingStoryTitles = new Set(existingStories.map((s) => s.title));
292	  const existingSeriesByTitle = new Map(
293	    existingSeries.map((s) => [s.title, s.id]),
294	  );
295	
296	  // 3. Stories
297	  console.log('\nCreating stories...');
298	  for (const spec of STORIES) {
299	    if (existingStoryTitles.has(spec.title)) {
300	      console.log(`  · skipped (exists)  ${spec.title}`);
301	      continue;
302	    }
303	    const tagIds = resolveTagIds(spec.tagNames);
304	    try {
305	      const created = await api<{ id: string; title: string }>(
306	        '/admin/stories',
307	        {
308	          method: 'POST',
309	          body: JSON.stringify({
310	            title: spec.title,
311	            content: spec.content,
312	            excerpt: spec.excerpt,
313	            estimatedReadMinutes: spec.estimatedReadMinutes,
314	            isAuthorsChoice: !!spec.authorsChoice,
315	            authorsNote: spec.authorsChoice?.note,
316	            tagIds,
317	          }),
318	        },
319	      );
320	
321	      if (spec.publish) {
322	        await api(`/admin/stories/${created.id}/publish`, { method: 'PATCH' });
323	      }
324	
325	      console.log(
326	        `  ${spec.publish ? '✓ published' : '· draft   '}  ${spec.title}`,
327	      );
328	    } catch (err) {
329	      console.error(`  ✗ ${spec.title}: ${(err as Error).message}`);
330	    }
331	  }
332	
333	  // 4. Series + chapters
334	  console.log('\nCreating series + chapters...');
335	  for (const seriesSpec of SERIES_SPECS) {
336	    const tagIds = resolveTagIds(seriesSpec.tagNames);
337	    try {
338	      let seriesId = existingSeriesByTitle.get(seriesSpec.title);
339	      if (seriesId) {

341	      } else {

347	              title: seriesSpec.title,

Faker is not currently installed. The plan will need to add `@faker-js/faker` as a devDependency. (Task tools aren't relevant here - this is a single planning task.)

I have enough context now. Let me synthesize the plan.

cliArgs: --confirm=dev (required; without it the script prints a warning + exits 1)
--purge (deletes ONLY rows whose title starts with the [seed-dev] marker; mutually exclusive with seeding)
--dry-run (prints counts + first 5 titles per type that would insert, no DB writes)
--seed=<int> (optional faker seed for reproducible runs; default = Date.now())
safetyGuards: Hard env-guard: refuses to run unless process.env.LUCIFER_ENV === 'dev'. Logs the actual value seen + exits 1.

Defensive DATABASE_URL check: if the URL contains 'prod', 'production', 'render.com', 'neon.tech', or any non-localhost host, abort with a loud red error before any write (extra belt-and-braces beyond LUCIFER_ENV).
Requires --confirm=dev. Without it, prints a 6-line warning explaining what the script does + that it writes garbage to the DB, then exits 1.

All seeded rows are tagged with the literal title prefix '[seed-dev] ' (Story.title, Series.title, Chapter.title). Cleaner than adding a schema column for a dev-only concern; survives every Prisma query as a plain string and is trivially LIKE-searchable.

Idempotent re-runs: before inserting, the script counts existing rows whose title starts with '[seed-dev] '. If count > 0 and --purge wasn't passed, it refuses to seed and tells the user to run --purge first (avoids the 'I ran it twice and now I have 100 stories' footgun).

--purge only deletes rows matching `title startsWith '[seed-dev] '`. Uses prisma.story.deleteMany({ where: { title: { startsWith: '[seed-dev] ' } } }) — junction tables (StoryTag/SeriesTag/ChapterTag) and Notes cascade via existing onDelete: Cascade. Chapters cascade when their Series is deleted.
--dry-run short-circuits before every prisma write. Each generator function still runs (so titles + counts are real), but the prisma.$transaction call is skipped and we log the plan instead.

Single top-level prisma.$transaction wraps every insert so a mid-script crash leaves zero partial rows. The transaction timeout is bumped to 120_000 ms because 50+ stories × up-to-10k-word bodies can be slow on a cold local DB.
Process exit codes are strict: 0 success, 1 guard failure, 2 mid-run runtime error. Lets CI / pre-commit hooks distinguish 'you ran it wrong' from 'the DB is broken'.
All console output is prefixed with '[seed-dev]' so it's grep-able in a busy terminal.

contentVolume.chaptersPerSeries: random integer in [3, 8] inclusive, drawn per-series via faker.number.int({ min: 3, max: 8 }) — empirically averages 5.5, so ~44 chapters across 8 series (within the requested 40–60 envelope)

input.markerStrategy: Title prefix '[seed-dev] ' on every Story, Series, and Chapter. Chosen over a dedicated schema column because (a) it requires zero migration, (b) it's visible to a human poking at the DB without reading code, (c) Prisma's `startsWith` filter makes purge a one-liner, and (d) it gracefully no-ops if the marker convention is ever changed (old rows stay discoverable). The prefix is exported as a top-level const SEED_MARKER = '[seed-dev] ' so the seed and purge paths can never drift.
input.purgeLogic: "On --purge, run inside a single prisma.$transaction: (1) delete all Chapter rows whose seriesId belongs to a Series with title startsWith SEED_MARKER (Prisma can't startsWith-filter across relations in deleteMany, so do this in two steps: findMany the matching series ids, then deleteMany chapters where seriesId in those ids), (2) delete all Series rows with title startsWith SEED_MARKER (cascades remaining chapters + SeriesTag rows + Follow rows), (3) delete all Story rows with title startsWith SEED_MARKER (cascades StoryTag + Note rows). Likes / ReadSessions / ReadingPositions / SavedContent are polymorphic with no FK — but a fresh dev DB won't have any pointing at seed rows, and the script logs a one-line warning telling the operator to manually clean those tables if they've been populated. Print a summary line: '[seed-dev] purged: N stories, M series, K chapters'. Exit 0."
input.tagSelectionAlgorithm: "At script start, prisma.tag.findMany() pulls the full taxonomy once and splits it into safeTags (isAdult=false) and adultTags (isAdult=true). For each story / series / chapter, pick a count in [3, 6] via faker.number.int. Then for each pick, with probability 0.7 draw from safeTags else from adultTags — this mirrors the rough real-site distribution (most content is Tier-1-only with an occasional Tier-2/3 dusting). Use a Set to dedupe so a row can't pick the same tag twice. If the DB has fewer than 6 tags in either bucket, gracefully clamp to whatever's available and log a one-time warning. Build the join rows via the createMany inside the same transaction (StoryTag / SeriesTag / ChapterTag), not via nested writes, to avoid 50 round-trips."
input.titleGenerationApproach: "Hand-curated mood-word pools (MOOD_NOUNS ~30 entries like 'Lamplight', 'Threshold', 'Hollow', 'Cinder', 'Drawer', 'Bell', 'Mourning', 'Letter'; MOOD_ADJS ~25 entries like 'Borrowed', 'Hollow', 'Quiet', 'Brittle', 'Late', 'Soft', 'Forgotten') combined via 4 rotating templates: (1) `The ${MOOD_NOUN} of ${faker.person.firstName()}`, (2) `${MOOD_ADJ} ${MOOD_NOUN}`, (3) `${faker.word.adjective()} ${MOOD_NOUN}` with the faker word title-cased, (4) `After ${MOOD_NOUN}`. Template chosen per row by faker.helpers.arrayElement. Result feels brand-aligned (echoes the existing 'On Lamplight', 'Borrowed Mornings', 'Hollow Sundays' tone) without literally copying any extant title — every word is either faker-generated or from a 100% original hand-pool. Final output is `${SEED_MARKER}${generatedTitle}`. Collision-resistant: appends a numeric suffix '(2)', '(3)'… if a freshly-generated title already exists in the in-script Set of generated titles."
input.excerptGenerationApproach: "faker.lorem.sentences(3) for the bulk, prefixed with one of an EVOCATIVE_OPENERS pool (~12 entries like 'A meditation on', 'A small confession about', 'Some nights are', 'In the space between', 'A letter never sent about'). Result reads like a moody literary blurb and is 100% derived from faker output + the hand-pool — no source material involved. Excerpts cap at 240 chars (truncate on word boundary + add ellipsis) so they fit the existing UI."
input.bodyGenerationApproach: "For each row, pick a target word count via faker.number.int({ min: 500, max: 10000 }) — uniform distribution gives the GSAP scroll-animation test a healthy spread of short/medium/long bodies. Loop faker.lorem.paragraph({ min: 4, max: 9 }) sentences and join with double-newlines until accumulated word count >= target. The animation work in PRs #187–#191 cares about page length and scroll-distance, not semantics, so pure lorem is correct here. estimatedReadMinutes = Math.max(1, Math.round(wordCount / 220)) — 220 wpm is the project's established read-speed constant (matches what the live editor computes)."

Plan submitted. Key project-specific findings folded in:

- **Faker is NOT currently installed** in `backend/package.json` — the script will require adding `@faker-js/faker` as a devDependency (worth flagging in the PR description). The skeleton imports from `@faker-js/faker` (v8+ API: `faker.word.adjective()`, `faker.lorem.paragraph({ min, max })`, `faker.helpers.weightedArrayElement`, `faker.number.int`).
- **Script convention**: existing `backend/scripts/seed-tags.ts` and `seed-content.ts` are `ts-node --transpile-only` invocations registered in `package.json` scripts (`seed:tags`, `seed:content`). The new script slots in as `seed:dev` following the same pattern, also reading `backend/.env` via `dotenv`.
- **Schema differences from a typical setup**: `seed-content.ts` hits the live admin REST API (login + POST), but the new script talks to Prisma directly — that's the only way `--purge` and transactional inserts can be atomic, and it sidesteps the need for the dev server to be running.
- **Tag taxonomy reality**: tags are already split via `Tag.isAdult`, so the safe/adult bucket logic is a clean filter rather than tier parsing.
- **Marker choice**: title prefix `[seed-dev] ` rather than a schema column — no migration required, visible in DB inspections, `startsWith` makes purge trivial.
- **Polymorphic-orphan caveat**: `Like`/`SavedContent`/`ReadingPosition`/`ReadSession` use polymorphic `contentId` with no FK — purge can't auto-cascade them; the script logs a warning so the operator knows to clean manually if a dev session has populated those tables.
